clue.text: I'm generous with receptacle filled for drinking

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: the word for generous is filled with the receptacle, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a big-hearted, big person is generous
a bin is a receptacle for rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of their generosity in topping up a vessel so everyone can drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'generous' looks like it describes the speaker, but it is a synonym piece; 'filled' signals the container, making BIBING.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbibe is to drink, so taking in liquor or liquid is the same activity.

clue.text: Wagnerian heroine that is betrayed, being captured

indicators.note: the word for betrayed is captured inside the abbreviation for that is

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is
sold, as in sold out, means betrayed

explanation.surface: An operatic heroine is betrayed and taken prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'betrayed' reads as describing the heroine's fate, which fits Wagner's tragic story; 'being captured' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tristan's lover in Wagner's opera is a heroine of that composer's work.

clue.text: Support hospital facilities in recession

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
wards are the rooms where hospital patients are housed

explanation.surface: Funding for hospital facilities during an economic recession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recession' suggests an economic slump; here it means moving back.
explanation.definitionFit: Recession is the act of going back or receding, so moving in recession is moving in reverse.

clue.text: Strong defence of good French and Italian wine imported

indicators.note: imported means the wine is brought into the French word

parts.note: bon is French for good
Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont in Italy

explanation.surface: A fortification guarded by fine French and Italian imported wines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imported' fits the wine surface but signals the container; 'good French' means the French word for good.
explanation.definitionFit: A bastion is a projecting part of a fortification, so a strong defensive point.

clue.text: Corners king shortly moving up to trap it

indicators.note: to trap means the letter for the king is caught inside the other word
in a down clue, moving up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: soon means shortly
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: In chess, a king soon moves up and is trapped in a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving up' turns SOON round to NOOS, and 'to trap' puts K inside it; 'it' refers back to the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Nooks are recesses or out-of-the-way corners of a room.

clue.text: Recalled reductions company offered for plastering

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the word for reductions is turned round

parts.note: cuts are reductions in spending

explanation.surface: A firm brings back its price cuts, offering them on building plasterwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' reads as a product recall, but signals the reversal, making STUC.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine plaster rendering used on walls and ceilings, so it is a kind of plastering.

clue.text: Hugely successful movie

parts.note: James Cameron's 1997 film about the sinking liner was a box-office record breaker, and its name also means huge

explanation.surface: A blockbuster film.
explanation.walkthrough: The film's title is also an adjective meaning enormous, which 'Hugely' hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: Cameron's film about the doomed ocean liner was one of the biggest box-office hits ever.

clue.text: Conservative competent to deliver message

parts.note: able means competent

explanation.surface: A capable Tory politician is sent to deliver a message.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable is a telegram, a message sent by wire.

clue.text: It's obvious the vessel had to capsize

parts.note: overt means open and obvious
an urn is a vessel, such as a vase

explanation.surface: It was plain that the ship was going to turn over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship; it is a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: To capsize is to turn over or upset, the same as to overturn.

clue.text: Some make mistakes with English flower-beds

definitions.note: plural, but the answer names a single garden laid out as an arrangement of beds

parts.note: part means some of something
to err is to make mistakes

explanation.surface: Some gardeners blunder in planting English flower-beds.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal garden of ornamental beds arranged in a pattern is made up of flower-beds.

clue.text: Board that's only available once in a while?

definitions.text: Board that's only available once in a while?

parts.words: Board that's only available once in a while?
parts.note: a board here is a flat piece of furniture you eat or rest things on, and one that is put out only now and then is a small side table

explanation.surface: An advertisement for a committee or a meal service that rarely opens its doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' suggests a committee or meals; it is the flat top of a small piece of furniture, and 'once in a while' gives its descriptive first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A small occasional piece of furniture is brought out as needed, so the clue's 'only now and then' describes its name literally.

clue.text: Certain properties of the same sort of wires

definitions.note: plural, matching the answer: goods brought to a marriage

parts.note: DO, short for ditto, means the same again

indicators.note: sort of means the word wires is put in another order

explanation.surface: A technical note on properties shared by wiring of one type.
explanation.walkthrough: DO is ditto, written in lists to mean 'the same'. 'sort of' rearranges WIRES to WRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's marriage portion is property brought to the union, so these are particular properties.

clue.text: One going straight on the circle line?

definitions.text: One going straight on the circle line?

parts.words: One going straight on the circle line?
parts.note: in geometry a straight line that just touches a circle at one point carries on straight from it

explanation.surface: A traveller on the London Underground's Circle line who does not change trains.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle line is a London Underground route; here it is a geometric circle, and the line meets it once and goes straight on.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometric line touching a curve at a single point continues straight, as the clue describes.

clue.text: One digging into large plate

definitions.meaning: someone or something that cuts ditches
a wooden platter once used for serving food

explanation.surface: A digger tucking into a big plate of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A digging machine or worker cuts ditches; and a medieval wooden platter for meat shares the same name.

clue.text: Is it enjoyed by the jet set?

definitions.text: Is it enjoyed by the jet set?

parts.words: Is it enjoyed by the jet set?
parts.note: the jet set are wealthy travellers who live glamorously, and flying in jets they also live well above the ground

explanation.surface: A question about what wealthy international travellers enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: The jet set live luxuriously, and in their planes they also live up in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashionable, extravagant living among the rich is what the jet set enjoy.

clue.text: Sighed audibly, with show of hesitation, being served alcohol

indicators.note: audibly means the word sighed is taken for how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like CID
er is the sound people make when they hesitate

explanation.surface: Someone sighs and hesitates before being handed a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: SIGHED is said aloud as CID; add ER and the spoken result is the apple drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The fermented apple drink is alcoholic, so it is a kind of alcohol.

clue.text: Arrange to provide of formal clothing

parts.note: to dress is to arrange, as in dressing a shop window or a line of troops
suit can mean to provide or furnish, as in old usage 'suited with clothes'

explanation.surface: Someone arranges for formal clothing to be supplied.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads oddly ('to provide of'); 'to' and 'of' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening wear for men, such as a tailcoat outfit, is formal clothing.

clue.text: Supply different cage for a time for unusual mammal

indicators.note: cage means the rearranged letters enclose the other pieces
different means the letters of supply are put in another order

explanation.surface: A zoo plans a new temporary cage for a strange animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges SUPPLY to PLYPUS, and 'cage' puts A and T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The duck-billed, egg-laying Australian creature is a famously odd mammal.

clue.text: Rope in young woman to introduce Oscar

parts.note: a lass is a young woman
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone recruits a girl to present Oscar to the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rope in' looks like 'persuade'; it is the definition, to catch with a looped rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch an animal with a noosed rope is to throw a loop at it, as cowboys do.

clue.text: Could be endlessly looming over us?

definitions.text: Could be endlessly looming over us?

indicators.note: could be means the letters may become something else when rearranged
endlessly means the word looming loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Something might be menacingly hanging over us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts LOOMING to OOMIN; 'Could be' rearranges OOMIN and US. The whole clue describes a threat.
explanation.definitionFit: Threatening and foreboding things seem to hang over us, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: See endless danger when they're thrown?

definitions.text: See endless danger when they're thrown?

indicators.note: thrown means the letters are tossed into a new order
endless means the word see loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A warning that throwing certain objects brings unending peril.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts SEE to SE; 'thrown' shuffles SE and DANGER into the answer, and the whole clue describes hand bombs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand-thrown bombs are dangerous once lobbed, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: A Greek involved in check-up is more irate

indicators.note: involved in means the abbreviation for Greek is caught up inside the other word
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain

explanation.surface: A Greek patient caught up in a medical check-up is getting crosser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'check-up' looks like a medical examination; split, 'up' turns the synonym of check to NIER, and 'involved in' places the Greek abbreviation within it.
explanation.definitionFit: More cross or more furious is more irate.

clue.text: But it sounds like smokers have abandoned it

definitions.text: But it sounds like smokers have abandoned it

parts.words: But it sounds like smokers have abandoned it
parts.note: the word but sounds like butt, the stub of a cigarette that smokers throw away

explanation.surface: Someone notes that smokers seem to have given up on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But' looks like a conjunction; said aloud it is butt, a cigarette stub, which the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: The discarded stub of a cigarette is what a smoker leaves behind, a butt.

clue.text: Four involved in hearing may appear unimportant

indicators.note: involved in means the numeral is wrapped up inside the other word

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four people caught up in a court hearing seem minor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' suggests sound, but it is a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trifling and of little consequence is unimportant.

clue.text: One hour in the morning to make pilgrim's garment

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
am is the abbreviation for ante meridiem, the morning

explanation.surface: Getting up an hour early to make a pilgrim's robe.
explanation.walkthrough: The ihram is the white garment worn by Muslim pilgrims to Mecca.
explanation.definitionFit: Muslim men wear two unsewn white cloths for the hajj, a pilgrim's dress.

clue.text: Article on Strindberg seen in state capital

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the other piece

parts.note: August Strindberg was a Swedish playwright
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about the Swedish dramatist appears in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts A after AUGUST. Augusta is the capital of the US state of Maine.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta is the seat of government of Maine, a US state.

clue.text: Some expatriates in old apartments in Rome

indicators.note: some means only part of the word expatriates is taken

explanation.surface: Some foreign residents live in ancient flats in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apartments' suggests flats; they are the central halls of Roman houses.
explanation.definitionFit: The central court of an ancient Roman house was a principal room, so these are old Roman apartments.

clue.text: A day bed, maybe?

parts.note: a day can be read as a span of time, and a bed is an item for a home, so the phrase describes antique household items of a particular era

explanation.surface: A couch for daytime napping is offered as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: A day bed is a couch; split as 'a day' (a span of time) and 'bed' (an item of household fittings) it describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Antique household items in the style of a historic era are named after that era, and a day bed is one example.

clue.text: Uncle, perhaps very large, has a savoury snack

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the USA, so Sam is an uncle
OS is the abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: An overweight uncle has a savoury snack.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle Sam is the cartoon figure for the United States; OS (outsize) is a clothing size meaning very large.
explanation.definitionFit: The fried pastry triangle with a spiced filling is a savoury snack from South Asia.

clue.text: Depart, or move about, as it's mindlessly repeated

indicators.note: move about means these letters shift into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone told to leave or move around keeps repeating it without thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move about' rearranges DEPART and OR.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy words without understanding, like a talking bird, is to repeat them mindlessly.
